cells.tense: You are steering from your sense of what is fair.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take a choice you have already lived out and count what it left in your hands, plainly, the way you would count anything else.
cells.core:
You have come through something and it is done, and you are steering from what your own sense of fairness tells you is right. When a choice sits open, you can move on it without counting the cost to yourself first, and that shows in what people bring you. The direction you set from here carries the weight of what it took to get here, and it is steady.

On the next choice that feels finished, stop and look at what it actually made. Not what you gave up for it — what it produced. Gather the yield instead of gesturing at it, and tally the concrete thing your patience earned, whether or not you feel like it did.
cells.sheetLine: The direction you choose holds what it cost you.
cells.verb: weighing what's right and steering by it
cells.place: at the point of choosing a direction

cells.tense: You are already living in the outcome of a choice not yet made.
cells.act: let resources flow to the person who needs them
cells.ask: When you catch yourself running the future again this week, put something concrete into someone already under a decision — and finish it before the week does.
cells.core:
There is a ledger open for a decision you have already run in your head. You are bracing for the outcome, and the steering has turned into defense — what you will concede, what you will insist on, what will be owed either way. The moral accounting has a grip on the future, and the people caught in this with you can feel you carrying it.

Set the ledger down and put your strength somewhere it can land — one concrete thing, this week, for someone already under a decision. A ride, a meal, a call that ends something. Do it and finish it. The choice you cannot yet make will still be there, and you will have held someone up while you waited.
cells.sheetLine: The decision runs ahead of you and takes the room with it.
cells.verb: weighing what's right and steering by it
cells.place: at the point of choosing a direction

cells.tense: You are still waiting at a door with no handle.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Someone you know is stuck where you have already been. Point them at the way through you can see from here, say it once, and go back to your own road.
cells.core:
The direction is there and you are not stepping into it. Choices are offered and something in you holds back, and the hold is not cowardice — it is a pass you have not been able to make. The feeling underneath the compass has gone quiet, and from the outside it looks like you don't care which way the thing goes.

What gets you moving again is not more trying. Someone else is stuck at a passage you already found. Tell them the step you took first, then stop talking — the route you describe does something to you too while you are describing it, and you find a direction under your own feet again.
cells.sheetLine: The choice is open and you are not stepping through.
cells.verb: weighing what's right and steering by it
cells.place: at the point of choosing a direction

cells.tense: The steering is yours and the room is calling it the weather.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Over a few days, watch for the moments you steer a situation toward what feels fair, and mark them down afterward in your own words.
cells.core:
A choice is being made and the hand making it does not sign. When a direction has to be chosen, you are the one weighing it — checking what is fair, moving the smaller thing aside — and afterwards you'd say the situation demanded it or the group just found its way. That reading has something behind it: in the moment, you saw two roads and took one on purpose.

Much of what you know here came from somewhere else. Check one belief about what's right against the people you got it from, and if it still holds as yours, that counts. A compass you keep is worth more than one you inherited and went along with.
cells.sheetLine: The direction being chosen has your fingerprints on it.
cells.verb: weighing what's right and steering by it
cells.place: at the point of choosing a direction
